subject: general
question: In macroeconomic analysis, marginal propensity to save (MPS) is _________.

options.text: the change in savings per unit change in income of an individual
the savings per unit of a good
the savings per unit change in the price of a good
the savings per unit of income of an individual

solution:
The correct answer is __"**the change in savings per unit change in income of an individual**".__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **fraction** of increased **income** that is **saved **rather than **consumed** is known as the** marginal propensity to save** (MPS).
 
• MPS **fluctuates** **with income** and is generally greater at greater levels of income.
 
• MPS, a concept from **Keynesian macroeconomic theory**, is **computed by dividing** the change in income by the change in savings.
 
• The **Keynesian multiplier,** primarily explains the impact of additional funding or **government expenditure** as a **boost** to the economy, which is determined with the **aid of MPS**.
 
• The MPS of consumers can **help economic experts** predict how changes in government expenditure or **capital spending** would affect saving.
 
• A** savings line**, which has a slope due to the placement of change in savings on the** vertical y-axis** and change in income on the** horizontal x-axis**, is used to **represent MPS**.
 
• *Therefore, In macroeconomic analysis, marginal propensity to save (MPS) is the change in savings per unit change in income of an individual.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to **Keynesian economics**, economic **declines** can be addressed or **avoided by** utilizing proactive** public policy** to control consumer spending.
 
• **Keynes** was an outspoken **opponent of earlier economic views**, which he described as "mainstream economics," and he created his views in the aftermath of the **Great Depression.**
 
• The main **methods** advocated by Keynesian economics to steer the economy and combat poverty are **activist fiscal and financial policy**.
 
• Because labor demand curves drop downward similar to any other regular demand curve, **Keynesian theory contests** the claim made by certain academics that **lowering wages** can bring about a **reinstatement of full employment.**
